headline: Indian markets face pressure as RBI raises repo rate to 5.5% amid global inflation concerns

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: The RBI raised the repo rate to 5.5% for the first time in nearly four years under Governor Sanjay Malhotra
FPIs sold Rs 21,745 crore in the second half of September, targeting oil & gas, auto, and financial sectors
Global markets are weak as Asian stocks drop on inflation concerns and US Treasury yields climb
US Fed minutes signal another potential interest rate hike by the end of the year as inflation remains high
whatHappening: The Nifty 50 and Sensex closed significantly lower in the previous session following the RBI's rate hike announcement
The central bank has shifted its monetary policy stance to ‘calibrated tightening’ to manage price pressure
Home loan EMIs are expected to increase as a direct consequence of the higher repo rate
Adani Enterprises and Hindalco emerged as top losers in the market's recent downturn
summary: The Indian stock market is adjusting to a surprise RBI repo rate hike to 5.5% and a shift toward calibrated tightening. Sentiment is further weighed down by heavy FPI selling and weak global cues from both Asian and US markets. Major stocks like Hindalco and Adani Enterprises are under pressure as investors react to rising borrowing costs and persistent inflation.
